newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU threatens U.S. over textiles rules.
newsitem.headline: EU threatens U.S. over textiles rules.

text.p: The European Commission on Friday threatened to take the United States before the World Trade Organisation over rules it said were classifing European goods as being made in China or India.
"The European Commission has investigated...and concluded that without a satisfactory offer from the United States soon, it will complain formally," the EU executive said in a statement.
At issue, the Commission said, were U.S. rules of origin that classified goods such as Italian scarves, German furnishings or British cotton products as begin made elsewhere.

"America's origin rules say that even if a piece of grey cloth imported from China, India, Pakistan or elsewhere is cut, bleached, shrunk, dyed, printed or labelled in Europe, it does not benefit from EU origin (trade agrrangements)," it said.

"These rules could harm top European designers and clothing manufacturers either by resulting in quotas or by undermining quality European labels as a selling point among American consumers," the Commission said.
